title: Behind-the-Back Escape Dribble
description: Ball handlers practise the behind-the-back dribble as an escape move when a defender cuts off the crossover lane, with a passive defender for realism.

content.objective: Choose the behind-the-back escape dribble only when the crossover lane is truly cut off.
content.setup: A ball handler faces a defender who overplays one side, cutting off the easy crossover.
instructions: The ball handler attacks the overplayed side at a controlled pace.
When the defender cuts off that lane, the ball handler goes behind the back to escape to the other side.
Finish with two hard dribbles toward the rim after the escape.
Reset with the defender overplaying the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Only use the move when the direct path is actually blocked.
Keep the behind-the-back dribble tight to the body.
Accelerate immediately after completing the move.
commonMistakes: Using the move as a habit rather than a read.
Slowing down right after the escape instead of attacking.
Watching the ball instead of keeping the head up.
content.safety: Defenders apply token pressure only — no reaching in aggressively.
